Tracking issue for a bug listed on the roadmap. **Found by me, not reported** — filed here so it has a number, and so that closing it is what takes it off the page.

**Roadmap:** https://aaronified.github.io/tippani/roadmap.html#bug-legacy-exports

### What happens

1.1.1 made the catalogue export always write type: movie / type: show , which is what routes a file back to the right importer. Files exported by 1.1.0 or earlier were not rewritten, so a bare film export from then — no director, no collection, no character/actor/timestamp on any line — still carries nothing identifying it. Re-export it, or add a type: line by hand. Not fixable retroactively: a detector cannot infer what the file never recorded, so this one stays listed rather than pretending to be fixable.

open_bugs.body:
**Symptom.** After running for some hours the container reports **healthy** and its log looks
perfectly normal, but the app does not load in a browser. **Restarting the container fixes it.**
Seen twice on 2026-08-19, on 2.1.1 under Docker on a busy NAS.

The log at the point of failure is a clean startup and then nothing:

```
[integrity] running PRAGMA quick_check on /data/tippani.db
[integrity] OK — database passed quick_check
[fts] checking 5 full-text index(es) for corruption
[fts] books_fts OK … utterances_fts OK
tippani 2.1.1 (ghcr.io/aaronified/tippani)
config: data=/data tmdb(builtin=false) tls=false cookie_secure=false trusted_proxy=false
tippani listening on http://0.0.0.0:8080
```

## Two things make this much harder to diagnose than it should be, and both are defects in their own right

**1. `/healthz` proves the process is alive and nothing else.** The handler is
`w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)` — it touches no database, takes no lock and reads no state
(`internal/httpapi/server.go`). So a Docker healthcheck stays green for as long as the process can
accept a TCP connection, whatever is happening to real requests. "It says healthy" is not evidence the
app works, and right now it reads as though it were. **A health endpoint that cannot go red while the
app serves nothing is a health endpoint that reports the wrong thing.**

**2. A hung request logs nothing at all.** `logRequests` writes its summary line *after*
`next.ServeHTTP` returns, so a request that arrives and never completes produces no log entry — and
`/healthz` is skipped from logging entirely. An empty log after `listening` is therefore consistent
with *both* "no requests are arriving" and "requests are arriving and hanging", which are opposite
problems. There is no way to tell them apart from the log as it stands.

## Candidate mechanisms — neither confirmed

**Connection-pool exhaustion.** `SetMaxOpenConns(4)` with `busy_timeout(5000)`
(`internal/store/store.go`). The busy timeout bounds how long a *statement* waits for the write lock,
but it does not bound how long a request waits for a *connection*: `database/sql` queues on the pool
and only gives up when the request context is cancelled. A browser request carries no deadline, so
four stuck connections are enough to make every subsequent request hang for ever while the process
stays alive and healthy. A restart clears it, which matches the symptom exactly.

**The host's port publish.** Earlier the same day, several unrelated containers on the same box
(including Transmission) were simultaneously unreachable and recovered on their own after a few
minutes, which pointed at host saturation rather than at any one app. A restart re-creates Docker's
userland proxy, so it would also clear this. This is the reason the report says "candidate": it has
not been ruled out.

## What would tell them apart, next time it happens — before restarting

```bash
curl -sS -m 5 -o /dev/null -w 'host %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3015/healthz   # host side
docker exec tippani wget -T 5 -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz                    # inside
curl -sS -m 20 -o /dev/null -w 'api %{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3015/api/auth/status
```

If `/healthz` answers on both and `/api/auth/status` hangs, it is the app and almost certainly the
pool. If `/healthz` fails from the host but answers inside the container, it is the port publish.
Also worth capturing before the restart: `docker exec tippani kill -QUIT 1` dumps every goroutine
stack to the log, which names whatever is holding the connections.

## Fixes worth making regardless of the root cause

- **Give `/healthz` something to check** — a `SELECT 1` on a short context, so a wedged database makes
  the container unhealthy instead of leaving it green. Cheap, and it is the difference between an
  operator being told and an operator guessing.
- **Log the request on the way in as well as on the way out**, at trace level or with an in-flight
  count, so "arrived and hung" and "never arrived" stop looking identical.
- **Bound the wait for a connection** — a request context deadline, so an exhausted pool returns 503
  rather than hanging for ever. A visible error beats a spinner.
- **Report in-flight requests and pool stats somewhere** (`db.Stats()` is free), so exhaustion is
  observable rather than inferred.
open_bugs.title: Container reports healthy but serves nothing until restarted; /healthz cannot detect it
